decision.summary: A routine bedroom window repair has had no visit booked since the contractor was assigned on 1 March, despite three reminders. I asked the tenant whether he has been in touch and for her availability, put the job on hold until 12 March, and escalated the contractor non-response and the approval gap to maintenance.

answers.answer: Routine window repair; Oscar Turner assigned 1 Mar but has not booked a visit despite 3 email+SMS reminders. No visit, quote or valid landlord approval recorded for this property.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Email to tenant Eliza Jenkins asking whether the contractor has been in touch and for her availability (sent); internal escalation to maintenance to phone or reassign the contractor.

answers.answer: Yes, a low-priority one. Maintenance needs to decide whether to reassign the contractor and to re-confirm landlord approval, because the landlord's only reply named a different property (Flat 18, 88 Alder Lane).

args.body: Hi Eliza, sorry for the wait with your bedroom window. We asked our contractor, Oscar Turner, to contact you on 1 March and he has not yet confirmed a visit, so we are following this up with our team today. Has he been in touch with you? If so, please tell us the date. If not, please let us know which days and times suit you for a visit (we'll give 24 hours' notice). Our target for routine repairs is within 14 days, and we will confirm a date once we have one. Thank you for your patience.
